subject: Re: Vulnerability management clarifications for Redwood RFP - Evershore
messages:
From: Liam Porter <liam.porter@evershore.com>

Cc: security@evershore.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vulnerability management clarifications for Redwood RFP - Evershore

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for participating in our RFP. We have a handful of follow-up clarifications we need on your vulnerability management (SAST/DAST) and related assurance artefacts before the evaluation committee convenes next week. Can you confirm the following items and return any evidence you can share under NDA?

1) SAST cadence and gate policy (PR-level, pre-merge, branch scanning) and toolchain.
2) DAST scope — authenticated vs unauthenticated testing, frequency, and remediation SLAs.
3) Pen test cadence, scope (blackbox/greybox), and summary of last full-engagement findings and mitigations.
4) Patch SLAs for critical/high/medium findings in both managed hosted runtime and private deployments.
5) SBOM availability and whether you include nested transitive dependencies and license info.

If possible, attach an executive summary or samples (SBOM sample, pen-test executive summary). We can treat any attachments as confidential under the NDA term sheet we already signed.

We'd ideally like responses by EOD Thu, Mar 25 to feed into our scoring. Happy to take a short follow-up call if that helps.

Regards,
Liam Porter
Director, Security Evaluation
Evershore Capital

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Vulnerability management clarifications for Redwood RFP - Evershore

Liam — per our note, please find concise answers below and attached artifacts. Attachments: 20270322-Redwood-SAST-DAST-Exec-Summary.pdf, SBOM-sample-Redwood-202703.zip, pen-test-summary-202611.pdf

SUMMARY ANSWERS (high level)
- SAST: We run automated SAST in CI on every pull request (pre-merge) using an aggregation of open-source scanners (Semgrep + custom rules) and commercial scanners for third-party dependencies. Full repo-level scans run weekly. Policy: PRs with new high or critical findings are blocked until triage; owners have 48 hours to acknowledge and a mitigation/plan within 5 business days.

- DAST: Production-like staging DAST runs are scheduled weekly against our public API surfaces and nightly smoke DAST on critical endpoints. Authenticated DAST is performed monthly for full-scope apps where credentialed tests are safe; otherwise, we run authenticated tests in isolated staging. Findings severity is mapped to our patch SLAs (see below).

- Pen Test: Third-party red-team / pentest engagements occur annually and after material architecture changes. Typical scope: greybox testing (auth when required), API and admin surfaces, and host/container configuration checks. The attached pen-test executive summary is a redacted high-level report from Nov 2026 — it includes findings, CVE mappings, and mitigations completed.

- Patch SLAs (standard):
  * Critical (actively exploited / CVSS >= 9): Acknowledgement within 4 hours, mitigation plan within 48–72 hours; permanent remediation targeted within 14 days or via configuration fallback if immediate patching risks availability.
  * High (CVSS 7–8.9): Acknowledgement within 24 hours, mitigation plan within 5 business days, remediation within 30 days.
  * Medium/Low: triaged per release cycle (30–90 days) with compensating controls where required.

- SBOM: We produce SBOMs per release (CycloneDX format) including direct and transitive dependencies and license metadata. For hosted customers we attach SBOMs to the release artifact; for private deployments we provide a downloadable SBOM bundle within 48 hours of release and can include it in our evidence package.

If you need formal SLA language for contracts or need the exact triage workflow (Jira playbook) I can loop in our security ops owner.

Regards,
Karthik
From: Liam Porter <liam.porter@evershore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@evershore.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vulnerability management clarifications for Redwood RFP - Evershore

Thanks Karthik — very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we mark the item as answered: 

1) SBOM: does the SBOM include hash values for each artifact and the version of the build toolchain? We need reproducible-element data for our internal supply chain attestation.
2) Pen test: does your typical greybox include authenticated API calls that exercise privilege escalation paths? If not, can you support an authenticated scope on Evershore-managed staging for a one-off engagement?

Also — we noted your critical SLA mentions fallback/config workarounds. For enterprise scoring we prefer contractual commitment to a remediation timeline; would Redwood consider a 7–10 day remediation SLA for critical items under a committed enterprise contract?

Best,
Liam
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Liam Porter <liam.porter@evershore.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vulnerability management clarifications for Redwood RFP - Evershore

Hi Liam — looping in procurement details. We can support enterprise SLA language for committed contracts; typical approach is:

- Base public offering: the patch commitment windows Karthik outlined (acknowledgement/plan windows) with best-effort remediation timelines.
- Enterprise reserved capacity / Private deployment: we agree to contractual remediation SLAs for Critical issues (enterprise addendum) — our standard negotiated window is 7 business days for permanent remediation or documented mitigation plus rollback plan.

I've attached a procurement checklist and an example SLA addendum for review (procurement-checklist-evershore.xlsx). If Evershore prefers, we can propose explicit compensation terms for SLA breaches in the addendum.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Liam Porter <liam.porter@evershore.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 14:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vulnerability management clarifications for Redwood RFP - Evershore

Liam — quick answers to your follow-ups:

1) SBOM: Yes — our CycloneDX SBOMs include SHA-256 hashes for packaged artifacts and a toolchain metadata block capturing build-tool version (compiler, packager) and build date for reproducibility. We can additionally provide git-commit/manifest references on request.

2) Pen test: Our standard greybox engagements do include authenticated flows that exercise privilege boundaries where safe. For Evershore we'd be happy to coordinate an authenticated engagement against a staging environment you provide (Evershore-managed staging) or use our isolated staging with redacted customer data. We'll need test accounts and scope definition before kickoff.

3) SLA commitment: We can include a contractual enterprise addendum with a 7-business-day remediation SLA for Critical findings (with a documented mitigation/rollback plan allowed within that window). Marissa will share the template.

Next step — if you're agreeable, Marissa and I can schedule a 30-minute sync to align on evidence transfer (signed NDA handling, drive share vs secure portal), and Neha can walk through the redacted pen-test executive summary. Would Thu 3/25 16:00 PT or Fri 3/26 09:00 PT work?

Thanks,
Karthik
